messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#1229] Rhadoop silver bullet for memory intensive calculation?
parts:
Hi 
I would recommend a hadoop mapreduce tutorial first to  answer questions about data and compute load distribution and then the RHadoop wiki to see how this is made available in R. For mahout questions, this is not the best venue but there are dedicated forums. Also the r-project.org HPC view could be of interest to you. Algorithms must be implemented to take advantage of the rmr2 API or  there is no advantage in loading the package. I think this is true of most parallel libraries for Hadoop and beyond, automatic parallelization is not something that anybody expects to become a common, general answer to performance issues in the foreseeable future. 

Antonio

On Sun, Dec 22, 2013 at 11:38 AM, Risto Saari <rist...@gmail.com> wrote:
Good points, agreed. I read this https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/wiki/plyrmr and other pages, and if i understood correctly some of the r functions are implement in rhadoop. I have used aws mr and 10 ec2 instances with good success.

Whats still a challenge if i have big vector and using something like r dist function i will have out if memory. I could not find if dist is implemented in rhadoop.

Unfortunately it isn't. If I understand correctly, you have an nxm matrix and you want to compute the euclidean or other distance beteen all pairs of rows of the matrix, which will result in a nxn matrix after executing some n^2 m multiplications. The nxm matrix can fit in memory but the nxn can not. I think a very similar problem is tackled in the kmeans example. There is a matrix of points and a matrix of centers and what is desired is computing all the distances between one point and one center. For you it just happens that the set of points and the set of centers is the same. So a program could look like

M #input matrix

mapreduce(scatter(to.dfs(M)), map  = function(k,v) distxy(M,v))

Where scatter is a utility to break down a data set into smaller parts, that helps with achieving a higher level of parallelism on smaller data sets. distxy is like diist but with two arguments. It's implemented as part of the kmeans example where it is called dist.fun. As usual with small data, large compute problems you will have to work a bit to make Hadoop do the right thing as far as number of map tasks and some such: Hadoop is designed for big  data application but has been pushed into either directions, just keep in mind that it's a bit more advanced stuff and defaults may not serve you very well. The above program is a sketch, I've never run it and its final from may depend on what you are going to do it afterward.

I am looking scale out when using r and rhadoop. Rapidminer had some hadoop specific stuf, but I think it did not have great success.

If memory begans a problem in r is there a clever way to workaround it?

This is more a RHadoop discussion group then a general scalability or big data one, so I am afraid we would veer off topic nor you would get the best answers by seeking this kind of information here. The range of solutions is huge and depends on algorithm, budget and many other factors.
There is a huge potential when r gets hadoop benefits, i hope all the best for the project!
